subject: Four warrants from three parallel agents - and the real reason the score collapses: the system throttles itself because it found no edge
body:
Four warrants shipped from three parallel investigations. Two of my own claims were wrong and
are corrected below, and one of the investigations stopped me making a genuinely harmful edit.

THE REAL EXPLANATION FOR WHY THE SCORE COLLAPSES. This is the finding of the session. The score is
not on the wrong scale - it is being throttled. The IC noise gate multiplies every weight by a factor
that floors at 0.40 when all the ICs are near zero, which is exactly the state your calibration
reports as "no per-regime edge". Then the total is multiplied by a sequence factor, by a damper with
a floor of 0.80, by another with a floor of 0.65, and by 0.92 in a contested value area, and finally
normalised against a reference computed from the same already-attenuated weights. Compounded, that is
roughly a tenth of raw. So the system suppresses its own score BECAUSE it diagnosed no edge, and is
then judged against a 50-point bar that assumes an unsuppressed score. The more certain it becomes
that it has no edge, the less able it is to ever produce a score that could prove otherwise.

CORRECTION ONE. The instrumentation I added earlier - the gates, the probability filter, the entry
comparison - sits in the LEGACY PRE-CALIBRATION path, which is skipped entirely once calibration
completes. Their zero hits were therefore not evidence about those gates. Nothing reached them
because the whole block is bypassed. I drew a conclusion their placement could not support.

CORRECTION TWO, and the important one. I told you MT4 had stripped the EA from your chart and it
needed restoring. That was wrong. The EA is attached, current and correct - on chart03, not chart02.
MT4 renumbers chart files by window order, and the id field proves the same chart simply moved. The
file I had backed up actually belonged to chart01, which is where my "the backup is empty too"
conclusion came from - I backed up the wrong file and then reasoned from it. If I had "restored" the
expert block into chart02, both charts being USDJPY M5 with the same magic number, you would have had
TWO copies of the EA running on one symbol, double calibration and interfering order loops. The
investigation caught it before I did.

WHAT SHIPPED:

The sample-floor contradiction is fixed - and there were TWO gates, not one, with the soft path being
the one that actually runs, so fixing only the one I found would have changed nothing.

The "weights out of bounds" thing I reported earlier was NOT a defect - the real range is 0.05 to 4.0
and everything observed was inside it; one comment block was serving two different contracts. But the
same sweep found a real one: a stage clamping to a narrower range than its siblings, firing precisely
on the weak regimes.

The calibration time budget now works under the tester - it was denominated in simulated time, and
one function is the abort condition for about twenty long-running loops.

Two unit conversions were missing in opposite directions, so I shipped both together; fixing either
alone would have moved the system a direction we could not predict.

And the single most misleading number in your logs is gone: the bar line was printing a threshold
that does not gate anything. That is why 57, 28 and 50 looked contradictory - they were different
variables, and the log showed the one that matters least.

Eighteen clean compiles today. Board unchanged at 17 met.

One thing that is your decision, not mine: the 50-point floor is the real lever on whether this
system trades at all, and the codebase carries an explicit, evidence-backed decision not to lower it
- because at a reachable threshold of 40 the measured expectancy was negative. Lowering it would
convert a silent halt into a system that trades at a measured loss.
